clean.title: Driveway and Turning Areas
clean.summary: Burbank Standard Plan BT-400 shows how to lay out circulation driveways and aisle geometry for angled parking in a private lot. Minimum driveway width is 13' for one-way traffic with parking angles of 45 to 90 degrees and 16' for 30 to 44 degrees, with 10' added for two-way traffic. It also gives an R=20' turning radius access driveway detail and rules for posts or obstructions beside stalls.
clean.notes:
Circulation driveways for various parking angles:
1. Driveway = 13' minimum (MIN.) for one-way traffic and parking angles of from 90 degrees to 45 degrees.
2. Driveway = 16' MIN. for one-way traffic and parking angles of from 30 degrees to 44 degrees.
3. The driveway dimension shall be increased by 10'-0" for two-way traffic.
4. Not less than bay widths shown on attached tables.

Notes (obstructions adjoining stalls):
1. Standard space shall be a minimum of 10' wide if post or obstruction is in cross-hatched area on either one or both sides.
2. End stalls shall be a minimum of 11' wide or the access aisle must extend 3' beyond the bay.
3. For compact spaces, the minimums shall be 1' less than the above requirements.
4. (See sheet 10 for angles of spaces less than 75 degrees.)

Circulation driveways note:
Add 9' to drive for two-way traffic or more than 20 cars in "C" zone or 40 cars in "R" or "M" zone.

clean.summary: Burbank Standard Plan BT-401 gives two charts relating basic stall width to the minimum access aisle width, one for standard cars (8'-6" to 9'-4" stalls with 27'-4" to 24'-0" aisles) and one for compact cars (7'-6" to 8'-4" stalls with 25'-4" to 22'-0" aisles). clean.notes:
Under the charts: Where parking adjoining the access aisle is a combination of standard size and compact size automobile spaces, Chart No. 1 shall be used for determination of minimum access aisle width.

Special requirements.

Driveway widths and locations:
A. 10' minimum in all zones.
B. 19' minimum when serving more than 40 cars in an "R" or "M" zone, or more than 20 cars in a "C" zone, or in lieu thereof there shall be two 10' minimum access driveways. Traffic Division approval for the location and size of driveways shall be obtained for every parking area or garage.

A. 20% maximum slope on driveway or ramp.
B. 10% maximum cross slope of a driveway or ramp.
C. 5% maximum slope in any direction in a parking stall.
D. Transition slopes are required when the slope of the driveway or ramp exceeds 10%. There shall be a maximum change in gradient of 10% in any 10 foot section of the driveway including the driveway approach within the street right of way, except that on a driveway sloping up from the property line the gradient within the first 5 feet from the property line shall not exceed 10%.

Parking stall location:
A. No parking stall is to be located so that an automobile is required to back onto a major or secondary highway.
B. No automobile is allowed to back from any lot onto a street unless the parking area or garage and the driveway leading to this parking serves no more than two dwelling units.

clean.title: Striping for Parking Stalls
clean.summary: Burbank Standard Plan BT-404 shows stripe layout and dimensions for standard and compact parking stalls, both angled and 90 degree. Standard stalls are 18' long with 7'-0" clear between stripes and compact stalls are 15' long with 6'-0" clear. Under B.M.C. 31-1417 stalls are double-striped with 4 inch stripes, white for standard cars and yellow (or white if marked COMPACT or SMALL CAR) for small cars.
clean.notes:
Standard parking stalls: 18' stall length. 7'-0" clear between stripes. Stall length 16'-0" minimum (MIN.) for 45 degrees and above, 15'-0" MIN. for less than 45 degrees (angled stalls). 16'-0" MIN. for 90 degree stalls.

Compact parking stalls: 15' stall length. 6'-0" clear between stripes. Stall length 13'-0" MIN. for 45 degrees and above, 12'-0" MIN. for less than 45 degrees (angled stalls). 13'-0" MIN. for 90 degree stalls.

Burbank Municipal Code (B.M.C.) 31-1417: Parking spaces shall be double-striped and access lanes clearly defined including directional arrows to guide internal movements. Striping for standard car spaces shall be white in color, whereas striping for small car spaces shall be yellow in color or may be painted white if marked "COMPACT" or "SMALL CAR". All painted stripes shall be 4" in width.

clean.summary: Burbank Standard Plan BT-405 shows where columns may and may not be placed next to angled parking stalls. Cross-hatched zones along the shared stall line, based on a 4' offset and an 8' length on 18' by 9' stalls, are kept free of columns, and no column may sit behind any part of a space. Angles below 65 degrees and from 65 to 75 degrees follow the layouts shown, and steeper angles use the 90 degree standard.

The lead-in from each loop is twisted clockwise, at least 2 turns per foot (TYP.), and runs down to the pullbox with four conductor ends labeled 1, 2, 3 and 4 at the bottom of each twisted pair.

Case 1 layout detail (bicycle lane): the two octagonal loops are drawn between the curb face and the stopline. Each loop is 3' wide, made up of three 1' segments, and the two loops are 3' apart. A 1' dimension is shown between the right loop and the stopline. Each loop is also dimensioned as three 1' segments vertically along its right side. The loop lead-in cuts (marked D-D) angle down from the loops and join at a single slot (marked E-E) that runs to the pullbox at the curb face. The lead-in start point is 3' from the stopline measured along the gutter. Callout 1 points at the curb termination where the slot crosses the curb face to the pullbox. Section cut markers A-A are shown at each loop, D-D on each angled lead-in and E-E on the common lead-in. Labels: stopline, gutter, curb face, pullbox.

Case 2 winding detail: two circular loops with three turns each. The left loop is a simple three-turn loop. The right loop has a three-turn circular winding with a diagonal slot cut across it carrying additional wire runs. Lead-ins are twisted as for Case 1 and end at conductors 1, 2, 3 and 4.

Case 2 layout detail (vehicle lane): two circular loops placed from the lane line. The dimensions along the lane line are 6' (left loop), 10' (gap between the loops), 6' (right loop) and 1' (to the stopline). The loops sit 2' below the lane line. Section cut C-C is at the left loop, A-A and B-B at the right loop, D-D on the angled lead-ins and E-E on the common lead-in that runs to the pullbox at the curb face. Callout 1 points at the curb termination. Labels: lane line, stopline, gutter, curb face, pullbox.

Saw-cut sections (all drawn as hatched slots with circular wire cross-sections and a maximum 1/8 inch (1/8" MAX, TYP.) fill below the pavement surface): Section A-A shows one column of 4 wires and uses note 3 for width and note 2 for depth (TYP.). Section B-B shows two columns of 4 wires (8 wires) in a wider slot and uses note 4 for width. Section C-C shows 3 wires and uses note 3. Section D-D shows 2 wires and uses note 3. Section E-E shows 4 wires in a column in a wider slot and uses note 4.

pages.text: CITY OF BURBANK DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC WORKS TRAFFIC DIVISION GENERAL TRAFFIC REQUIREMENTS It is the responsibility of the Contractor performing work on a public street to install and maintain the traffic control devices according to the latest edition of the California Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (California MUTCD) or Work Area Traffic Control Handbook (WATCH) to insure the safe movement of traffic and pedestrians through or around the work area and provide protection and safety to construction workers. The Contractor must submit a traffic control plan for approval when requested by the Traffic Division or when traffic handling cannot use a typical application in the latest California MUTCD or WATCH. Any revisions to the traffic control plans or requirements shall be approved by the Assistant Public Works Director-Traffic. All traffic control devices (signs, delineators, barricades, type K temporary railing, portable changeable message signs, etc.) shall conform to the Caltrans Standard Specifications, Section 12. All devices must be in place and shall be repaired, replaced, or cleaned as necessary until work is complete and traffic control is not required. Flashing arrow boards are mandatory for lane closures on any multi-lane street. If any barricades are to be in place at night, they shall be equipped with flashing/steady yellow warning lamps. On working days, all travel lanes shall be open between 6:00 a.m. and 8:30 a.m. and between 3.30 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. One travel lane in each direction shall be open at all times between 8:30 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. Any deviation of lane closure hours shall be approved by the Assistant Public Works Director-Traffic. If parking is impacted by traffic control, the Contractor shall post “TEMPORARY NO PARKING ANYTIME” signs at a minimum height of 3 feet and at least 5 working days before start of work. The Contractor may obtain signs from the Public Works Permit Counter. Once posted, the Contractor shall notify the Burbank Police Department Traffic Division, at (818) 238-3100 for approval and enforcement of posted signs. Vehicular and pedestrian access to adjacent properties shall be provided at all times. The contractor SHALL notify the City of Burbank Transportation Management Center 5 business days prior to installing any traffic control that reduces vehicular capacity on any signalized roadway within the City.
